Events.RelatedBody: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Aspire. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. Aspire Dashboard's unauthenticated NotFound route can permit telemetry deletion in both standalone and AppHost-hosted deployments. In standalone deployments using browser-token authentication, it can also expose the browser token. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/aspire/issues/22148 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Critical - **Score:** 9.1 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N` - **Weakness:** CWE-862 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Any supported OS - **Architectures:** x64, Arm64 ## Affected Packages ### Standalone Aspire Dashboard Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- Aspire Dashboard | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 Both 13.6.3 and 13.6.4 contain the unauthenticated NotFound route. ### Aspire Dashboard SDK packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-arm64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-musl-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-musl-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-arm64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-arm64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Aspire Dashboard releases through 13.6.4 are affected, whether deployed independently or launched by an Aspire AppHost. For an AppHost using Dashboard SDK packages, check the resolved Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk package versions against the affected ranges above. If the AppHost selects a CLI-bundled Dashboard or a custom Dashboard path, check the version of that Dashboard instead. Aspire ships independently of .NET; installing a .NET runtime or SDK update does not replace the Dashboard. ### How do I fix the issue? Update Aspire Dashboard to version 13.6.5 or later. Neither 13.6.3 nor 13.6.4 is a fixed upgrade target. For container deployments, explicitly set the Dashboard image to `mcr.microsoft.com/aspire/dashboard:13.6.5` and recreate or redeploy the container. Replace older version tags and nightly image references, including those in generated Docker Compose or Kubernetes manifests, with this fixed stable image. Updating AppHost package references alone does not replace an image reference in an existing deployment manifest. For an AppHost using Dashboard SDK packages, update any explicit Aspire.Hosting.AppHost version, including a central package version, to 13.6.5 or later. If that reference is supplied implicitly by Aspire.AppHost.Sdk, update the SDK reference to 13.6.5 or later instead. Restore and rebuild the AppHost, verify that its resolved Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk packages are 13.6.5 or later, and restart the AppHost to run the updated Dashboard. If your AppHost selects a CLI-bundled Dashboard or a custom Dashboard path, update the Dashboard in that selected bundle or location to 13.6.5 or later and restart the AppHost. Updating AppHost package references alone does not replace that Dashboard. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue in the Aspire repository at https://github.com/microsoft/aspire. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Microsoft disclaims all warranties, either express or implied, including the warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-118740](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-118740) ### Acknowledgements - Weeraphat Srisutham ### Revisions V1.0 (November 10, 2026): Advisory published.

## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in ASP.NET Core. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. ASP.NET Core Identity scaffolding templates use the request-supplied email instead of the account's stored email for password-reset and confirmation messages. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/Scaffolding/issues/3959 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.1 (base score) - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-640 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Any supported OS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages Updating scaffolding packages/tools does not repair previously generated application code. Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc contains the affected templates. Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design is a parent package that brings in the MVC generator through a minimum-version dependency. For Design, applicability depends on the resolved MVC generator: a project that independently resolves a fixed MVC version does not become vulnerable merely because it retains an older Design reference. ### 8.0 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.23 | 8.0.24 [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.23 | 8.0.24 ### 9.0 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.12 | 9.0.13 [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.12 | 9.0.13 ### 10.0 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.2 | 10.0.3 [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.2 | 10.0.3 ### Additional known affected scaffolding prereleases These are exact known affected versions, not continuous prerelease intervals. Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold 20.3.0 Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet has been incorporated into Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold. Version 20.3.0 supports .NET 8, 9, 10 and 11. Install it as a .NET tool, not as a project package reference. The MVC and Design project packages use the separate fixed versions listed above; 20.3.0 is not a version of those packages. ### Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold 20.x Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold) | >= 20.0.0-preview.1.26156.3, <= 20.1.0 | 20.3.0 The 20.x tool contains the vulnerable Identity and Blazor templates for .NET 8.0 through 11.0. ### Affected legacy prereleases The following exact versions also contain affected templates: - [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) and [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design): `11.0.0-preview.1.26156.3` and `11.0.0-preview.1.26230.3`. - [Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet): `10.0.0-rc.1.25458.5` and `10.0.0-rc.1.25468.1`. Apply the generated-code repair below to applications created with these versions. For new scaffolding, use the Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold 20.3.0 tool, which supports .NET 8 through 11. Migrating to that tool is not an update to an MVC or Design project package reference and does not repair previously generated code. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Check both the installed scaffolding package/tool version and the code it generated. Applications generated with an affected template remain affected after the tool is updated unless their handlers are corrected. The `dotnet-aspnet-codegenerator` command loads generators from the application's dependencies. Check the project's Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design and Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc references against the versions above; updating only the command-line tool does not replace those project dependencies. For applications created with `dotnet new`, check the selected SDK with `dotnet --version` in the working directory. ### Describe the bug

After upgrading an existing Windows WinUI application from .NET 10 to .NET 11, NativeAOT compilation fails in an ML.NET generic virtual method. The same application previously built with NativeAOT on .NET 10 (reported by the application author). The .NET 11 failure was reproduced by directly rerunning ilc with the build-generated response file.

### Steps to reproduce

### Environment
- .NET SDK: 11.0.100
- Runtime / Microsoft.DotNet.ILCompiler: 11.0.0
- Compiler package repository commit: 297acf930fb0f5c07fd4e51d78e521b4ad2e5d1f (dotnet/dotnet)
- Windows, win-x64
- Target framework: net11.0-windows10.0.26100.0
- Microsoft.ML / Microsoft.ML.DataView: 5.0.1
- Microsoft.ML.TimeSeries: 5.0.1; Microsoft.ML.AutoML: 0.23.0
- Release build with PublishAot=true, PublishTrimmed=true, TrimMode=full


### Reproduction status / additional information
This is reproduced in an existing application; a standalone minimal reproduction is not yet available. No private application code or full response file is attached.

The failing ML.NET method forwards a generic virtual call to an underlying cursor. Adding --noscan to the same generated compiler invocation did not resolve the failure: that invocation exited with 0xC0000005 instead. No SDK fix or source-level workaround has been verified.


### Expected behavior

NativeAOT compilation succeeds, as it previously did with .NET 10, rather than throwing an internal compiler NotImplementedException.


### Actual behavior

Code generation failed for method '[Microsoft.ML.Data]Microsoft.ML.Data.DataViewConstructionUtils+DataViewBase`1+WrappedCursor<System.__Canon>.GetGetter<ReadOnlyMemory`1<char>>(Column)'

System.AggregateException
 ---> ILCompiler.CodeGenerationFailedException
 ---> System.NotImplementedException: The method or operation is not implemented.
   at ILCompiler.Compilation.ComputeConstantLookup(ReadyToRunHelperId, Object) in Compilation.cs:line 375
   at Internal.JitInterface.CorInfoImpl.ComputeLookup(Boolean, Object, ReadyToRunHelperId, MethodDesc, CORINFO_LOOKUP&) in CorInfoImpl.RyuJit.cs:line 338
   at Internal.JitInterface.CorInfoImpl.getCallInfo(CORINFO_RESOLVED_TOKEN&, CORINFO_RESOLVED_TOKEN*, CORINFO_METHOD_STRUCT_*, CORINFO_CALLINFO_FLAGS, CORINFO_CALL_INFO*) in CorInfoImpl.RyuJit.cs:line 1636


### Is this a regression?

[11.0 regression]

### Are there any workarounds?

_No response_

Issues.Title: [release/3.1] Reset current_no_gc_region_info after leaving no gc region implicitly
Issues.Body:
Backport https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/73602.

## Customer Impact
Customers reported occasional `System.InvalidOperationException` with message `The NoGCRegion mode was already in progress` when calling `GC.TryStartNoGCRegion`. This is preventing them from using this optimization and impacting their cold start latencies.

## Testing
Customers have tried the fix on .NET 6 overnight and reported the exception never appears again. Meanwhile, there is an unpatched machine and observed 72 exceptions of the same type in the same time interval, proving this does fix the bug.

## Risk
Low. This only impact customer using `TryStartNoGCRegion`, and this is the right thing to do.

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/coreclr) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. Issues.Title: Confusing behavior when using AssemblyInfo.cs
Issues.Body:
I'm completely perplexed.

I created a .Net Standard 2.0 library project.

I explicity added an AssemblyInfo.cs file, we need this because we use this utility to "stamp" our assemblies when we build them:

This is just mind blowing, is there no way we can do this seemingly simple operation any more if adopt .Net Standard?

Issues.Title: Questions about tagging within this repository / future versions
Issues.Body:
I was looking through this repository to determine if .NET Standard 2.1 libraries support default interface methods - it looks like they do, given the presence of `System.Runtime.CompilerServices.RuntimeFeature.DefaultImplementationsOfInterfaces`, as well as my own experimenting in VS 2019. It seems I was mistaken when thinking that this was not the case, so I'm glad this repository is easily accessible to determine this.

But while doing this, I found it difficult to determine what commits were included in this particular .NET Standard version. I see that there's a tag `v2.1.0-prerelease.19126.1`, as well as branches `release/2.0.0`, `release/3.0`, and `release/3.0-preview9`. One of the machines I tested VS 2019 on had a `netstandard.dll` assembly, itself targeting .NETStandard v2.1.0, with AssemblyInformationalVersion `1.1.0+a5b5f2e1e369972c8ff1e2183979fab6099f52ef`; this commit is part of the `release/3.0` branch. However, another machine had a same-named assembly, targeting .NETCoreApp v3.0 and AssemblyInformationalVersion `3.0.0+4ac4c0367003fe3973a3648eb0715ddb0e3bbcea`, and I don't see that commit hash in this repository.

Additionally, [this blog post](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/the-future-of-net-standard/) states that 2.1 will be the last version, but there is another prerelease tag `v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1` and [on GitHub](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/releases/tag/v2.2.0-prerelease.19564.1) it's labelled .NET 5.0 Preview 2.

So I have a few questions for understanding this repository:

1. Since .NET Standard 2.1 is released, are there plans to continue development in this repository for e.g. the shared BCL going forward with .NET 5+?
2. Are there multiple kinds of `netstandard.dll` for a single .NET Standard version? E.g. are there separate versions for .NET Framework to reference and for .NET Core / .NET 5+ to reference?
3. Do the tags / branch names in this repository correspond to a .NET Standard version or something else?
4. It looks like there are patch releases; are there patch versions of a single .NET Standard version?
5. Are there other repositories which are being used to create `netstandard.dll`?
6. Is there a way to determine, from the repository, which commit is the one used for a given release?

Thank you for your consideration.

Issues.Title: Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1
Issues.Body:
# Summary

.NET Standard version is not resolved correctly when a transitive dependency targets multiple .NET Standard versions.

# Environment

- Windows 10 (19042.746)
- .NET 5 SDK 5.0.201

# Minimal reproducible example
[bug.zip](https://github.com/dotnet/standard/files/6209239/bug.zip)

This is a three-project solution:
- `TestProject1` targeting `netcoreapp3.1`
- `ClassProject1` targeting `netstandard2.0`
- `ClassProject2` targeting *both* `netstandard2.0` and `netstandard2.1`

The project dependency chain is: `TestProject1 -> ClassProject1 -> ClassProject2`

A method (`ClassProject2Test1`) on `ClassProject2` is hidden behind a `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.

# The issue

The unit test failed with a `MissingMethodException`

```
[xUnit.net 00:00:00.38]     TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [FAIL]
  Failed TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1 [2 ms]
  Error Message:
   System.MissingMethodException : Method not found: 'Void ClassLibrary2.Class2.Class2Test1()'.
  Stack Trace:
     at ClassLibrary1.Class1.Class1Test1()
   at TestProject1.UnitTest1.Test1() in C:\Users\rex\source\netstandard-bug-repro\TestProject1\UnitTest1.cs:line 12
```

# Expected result

The compiler should have resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.0)*` 

# Actual result

The compiler resolved the chain as:

`TestProject1 (.NET Core 3.1) -> ClassProject1 (.NET Standard 2.0) -> *ClassProject2 (.NET Standard 2.1)*` 

Which causes the exception because the offending method, `ClassProject2Test1`, was hidden by the `#if NETSTANDARD2_0` preprocessor directive.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Issue with resolving between .NET Standard 2.0 and .NET Standard 2.1" (#1787)

Issues.Title: Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions
Issues.Body:
### Problem
There is a security vulnerability with the version of System.Text.RegularExpressions that is used by dotnet standard. The vulnerable version of System.Text.RegularExpressions is 4.3.0. Please see links below for the vulnerability documentation or discussion:

https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/en-US/vulnerability/CVE-2019-0820
https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/111
https://cve.mitre.org/cgi-bin/cvename.cgi?name=CVE-2019-0820
https://snyk.io/vuln/SNYK-DOTNET-SYSTEMTEXTREGULAREXPRESSIONS-174708
https://www.whitesourcesoftware.com/vulnerability-database/CVE-2019-0820

The dotnet commit that fixed the vulnerability is https://github.com/dotnet/corefx/commit/19d4b1163d8a03dd90ff5fd1785eea6305112545

### Issue:
We use whitesource and it has caught this issue with high severity. We don't consume System.Text.RegularExpressions directly but packages that use this. Therefore as a transitive dependency due to NetStandard library, which is being used by several other dotnet packages like Castle Windsor, MassTransit etc., Once an update is available the others could followup and update.

### Code:

[The latest version 2.0.3 of Net standard ](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) still seem to be using System.Text.RegularExpressions version 4.3.0 as per https://github.com/dotnet/standard/blob/master/src/apicompat/netstandard/netstandard.depproj

### Fix
Please update[ library](https://www.nuget.org/packages/NETStandard.Library/) targeting .netStandard 1.6 to update System.Text.RegularExpression package to latest secured version 4.3.1 to fix the security issue or kindly suggest alternatives.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Security Vulnerability due to System.Text.RegularExpressions" (#1786)

Issues.Title: linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem
Issues.Body:
Hello,

I am currently using .NET core 2.2.x and EF Core. 2.2.6. I have a function that returns a List<Animal> from the database with no issue. It returns 11 results. However, when I try to use `.Where(p => p.DeletedAt.GetValueOrDefault(DateTime.Now) => DateTime.Now).ToList()`, it still should return 11 results, however it returns 0. I also eliminated the possibility that there is something wrong with my where clause (logic) because it works perfectly on 4.6.1 EF Core 2.2.6. Furthermore, I confirmed that it is only where I am comparing a nullable type using that function and I am guessing that I missed a thread someone opened on this issue. I am aware .NET core 2.2 is not LTS. I also thought this goes here because it's not AFAIK, an EF core issue but rather an Ienumerable/Linq issue.

Update: As it turns out your notion of `DateTime.Now` getting evaluated twice is true. To rectify that, I will now be using `DateTime.Now.Date`. This is odd because this exact code works on 4.6.1. You're probably right. SMH. Thank you @GrabYourPitchforks! You may now close.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "linq using GetValueOrDefault  in Where clause problem" (#1792)

Issues.Title: Strong name signature not valid
Issues.Body:
Since I've ported a ClickOnce application from .NET Framework 4.6.1 to .NET Standard 2.0, the message _"Strong assembly name signature not valid for **Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll**"_ appears when trying to install or update the application. So the next step was to verify the assembly strong name by using the [Strong Name Tool](https://docs.microsoft.com/dotnet/framework/tools/sn-exe-strong-name-tool) to make sure, that everything is fine, but:

```sh
> sn.exe -v Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll

Microsoft (R) .NET Framework Strong Name Utility Version 4.0.30319.0
Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation. All rights reserved.

Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll is a delay-signed or test-signed assembly
```

Additional information:

- The assembly versions `161.46041.41` and `161.46367.54` ended up in the same result
- This issue looks very similar to [this](https://www.damirscorner.com/blog/posts/20140502-StrongNameValidationFailedSecurityException.html)
- @markingmyname / @olprod: The root package, which is required for [Server Management Objects (SMOs)](https://docs.microsoft.com/sql/relational-databases/server-management-objects-smo/overview-smo?view=sql-server-ver15), is:
  - [Microsoft.SqlServer.SqlManagementObjects](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.SqlServer.SqlManagementObjects)
    - Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment
      - Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Authoring
        - **Microsoft.SqlServer.Assessment.Types.dll**
- This issue appears on windows server machines but the software runs on different machines and I would like to avoid temporary workarounds such as editing the registry and activate the strong name bypass feature because of the forced validation on windows server machines

Issues.Title: System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings slow
Issues.Body:
_This issue has been moved from [a ticket on Developer Community](https://developercommunity2.visualstudio.com/t/SystemDrawingPrintingPrinterSettings-/890524)._ --- Hello I'm debugging a problem with the printer settings. Some calls are significant slower if the default printer is a network printer, even if I explicit set a local printer name. After studying referencesource I think I found the culprit. I call: var printerSettings = new System.Drawing.Printing.PrinterSettings(); printerSettings.PrinterName = "LOCALPRINTER"; // the next call is slow if the OS default printer is a network printer var res = printerSettings.DefaultPageSettings.PrinterResolution Internally FastDeviceCapabilities is called. FastDeviceCapabilities calls GetOutputPort. But GetOutput port return the port of the default printer and not the port of the given printer! In addition, DeviceCapabilities is then called with a wrong combination of printer name and port, don't know if this could lead to additional problems. Resolution: GetOutputPort should return the port of the given printer and not accessing the default printer at all. Best Regards, Raphael --- ### Original Comments #### Raphael Affolter on 1/20/2020, 04:03 AM:

I forgot to mention: .Net Framework 4.6.1

#### Feedback Bot on 1/20/2020, 06:51 PM:

We have directed your feedback to the appropriate engineering team for further evaluation. The team will review the feedback and notify you about the next steps.

#### Raphael Affolter on 2/7/2020, 08:39 AM:

Because we print a lot, we really suffer from this performance penalty.

Also reading PaperSizes and PaperSources from the printer settings is slow caused by the same problem.

Could you please inform me about a possible fix?

Best Regards,

Raphael

#### Raphael Affolter on 2/7/2020, 10:33 AM:

In my opinion the fix is easy: replace GetOutputPort by OutputPort in the call to

FastDeviceCapabilities.

Done.

If so, in order for us to investigate further, please provide more information by recording your repro steps via the Visual Studio Feedback Tool (Help -> Send Feedback -> Report A Problem). Issues.Title: Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF
Issues.Body:
I'm working on converting a large WPF solution's projects to SDK style and ran into some issues.

The solution is large with multiple projects(old style) all targeting .net452 and some nugets(some made by me) installed, targeting both .net452 and .netstandard2.1 This all seems to work fine, somehow the nuget manages to install the correct version targeting .net452.

I have decided to slowly convert the projects inside the solution to SDK style targeting .net452 and .netstandard2.1 just like the nugets.

This is where the problem starts, one project was converted so far that is referenced by multiple other projects. Localy everything seems to build and run fine, however when Azure DevOps(VS version 2019) is used to build the solution there are 2 scenarios:

1. The famous error message is shown:

                "Error CS0012: The type 'Object' is defined in an assembly that is not referenced. You must add a reference to assembly 
                 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0"

2. It builds fine but on app launch it crashes with:

                 "Could not load file or assembly 'netstandard, Version=2.1.0.0, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51' 
                 or one of its dependencies. The system cannot find the file specified."

I'm suspecting that the problem is related to referencing the SDK project, it looks like that somehow it references the .netstandard2.1 instead of the .net452.

The reason this is my suspicion is that if targetframework is set to only .net452 on the referenced project everything works fine. Google has led me to two possible solutions to tell the project what framework to use from the reference:

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj"
                  AdditionalProperties="TargetFramework=net452">
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
and

```
<ProjectReference Include="..\..\..\..\foo\foo.csproj">
      <SetTargetFramework>TargetFramework=net452</SetTargetFramework>
      <Project>{xxxxxx-xxxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxx-xxxxxxx}</Project>
      <<Name>foo</Name>
</ProjectReference>
```
This doesn't look like it's doing anything and the problem still persists. At the moment I ran out of ideas and I'm here asking for help. Please let me know what I'm doing wrong or what else I can try.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Build issues when referencing project that targets multiple frameworks C# WPF" (#1776)

Issues.Title: Migrate FabricBot Tasks to Config-as-Code
Issues.Body:
**TL;DR;** Requesting to add [FabricBot](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/fabricbot_overview) configuration associated with your repository to `.github/fabricbot.json`.

**Context**

FabricBot is now a [config-as-code-only](https://eng.ms/docs/products/1es-data-insights/merlinbot/extensions/bot-config-as-code) platform. As a result, while you can still use the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) to modify your FabricBot configuration, you can no longer save the changes. The only way to save changes to your configuration at the moment is to _export configuration_ from the portal and upload the exported configuration to `.github/fabricbot.json` in your repository. In this pull request, we are adding your FabricBot configuration to your repository at `.github/fabricbot.json` so that you can make changes to it going forward.

While the [FabricBot Configuration Portal](https://portal.fabricbot.ms/bot/?repo=dotnet/corefx) is the *only way* to modify your FabricBot configuration at the moment, we have a feature on our backlog to publish the JSON schema defining the structure of the FabricBot configuration file. With the JSON schema, you can (1) use a plaintext editor of your choice to modify the FabricBot configuration file and use the schema to validate the file after editing or (2) [configure](https://code.visualstudio.com/Docs/languages/json#_json-schemas-and-settings) VS Code to use the schema when editing FabricBot configuration file to take advantage of convenience features such as automatic code completion and field description on mouseover.

Issues.Title: Fix RSA OAEP decryption in OpenSSL with non-power-of-two keys lengths
Issues.Body:
## Customer Impact

A customer reported in dotnet/runtime#71607 that decrypting RSA OAEP with SHA2 and a 3072-bit key on Linux resulted in a OAEP de-padding error, while other platforms were able to perform these operations successfully.

Investigation in to the issue led to uncover that RSA OAEP decryption that uses the managed implementation does not work with non-power-of-two keys because we do not slice a rented buffer accordingly. The current implementation only works because `CryptoPool.Rent` happens to give back power-of-two arrays which are exactly the same size as the key.

The fix is to slice the data to the correct size.

This does not affect dotnet/runtime because the managed implementation of RSA OAEP is no longer used for OpenSSL RSA decryption. This change was introduced in dotnet/runtime#50063.

## Testing

Unit tests were introduced to test RSA OAEP encryption with a 3072-bit RSA key. These tests will be forward-ported to dotnet/runtime.

## Risk

Minimal. The change is localized and understood that a `Slice` was missing.

Issues.Body:
Branch [main](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/commits/main/) in `dotnet/roslyn` repo can't be mirrored from GitHub to Azure DevOps [main](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_git/dotnet-roslyn?version=GBmain&_a=history) via fast forward. 
There are unexpected commits in the target branch.
The branch is configured to be mirrored via fast forward only and is not expected to receive commits in the Azure DevOps clone.

Problem need to be **resolved to unblock the code flow**.

You can resolve the issue by unifying the SHA of the branches:
- merging the extra commits from the Azdo target branch into the source branch and pushing the changes to GitHub. 
    - Please make sure that the changes are not sensitive from security perspective!
- reverting the extra commits in the Azdo target branch.
- checking the logs of the mirroring process in the [mirroring pipeline](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_build?definitionId=1387).
- you can disable the mirroring of the branch in the [configuration file](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_git/dotnet-mirroring?path=/dnceng-subscriptions.jsonc).
- you can ask @dotnet/dnceng for help or read the [documentation](https://dev.azure.com/dnceng/internal/_git/dotnet-mirroring?path=/README.md).

Please close this issue once the problem is resolved.

Issues.Title: Renamer.RenameSymbolAsync shadows a captured primary-constructor parameter without reporting a conflict
Issues.Body:
<!-- issue-pr-loop -->
## Summary

Renaming an interface implementation's method parameter to the same name as a captured primary-constructor parameter changes the binding of an existing reference and introduces CS1061. This also affects analyzer code fixes that call the rename API: previously compilable source becomes uncompilable without a conflict annotation.

**Version Used**: .NET SDK 11.0.100; `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Workspaces, Version=5.12.0.0` shipped in its `DotnetTools/dotnet-format` directory; macOS arm64. The initial report was reproduced on Windows x64 with the same SDK. The direct API reproduction below does not use an analyzer.

**Steps to Reproduce**:

Create `global.json` with `{"sdk":{"version":"11.0.100","rollForward":"disable"}}`, then create `Logger.txt`:

```csharp
using System;

public interface ILogger
{
    void Log(Func<string> formatter);
}

public interface IFormatter
{
    string GetLogIssueCommand();
}

public sealed class Logger(IFormatter formatter) : ILogger
{
    public void Log(Func<string> messageFormatter)
    {
        Console.WriteLine(formatter.GetLogIssueCommand());
        Console.WriteLine(messageFormatter());
    }
}
```

Create `Rename.csproj` (uses the exact SDK-hosted rename assemblies):

```xml
<Project Sdk="Microsoft.NET.Sdk"><PropertyGroup><TargetFramework>net11.0</TargetFramework><OutputType>Exe</OutputType></PropertyGroup><ItemGroup><Reference Include="$(MSBuildSDKsPath)/../DotnetTools/dotnet-format/*.dll"/><Reference Include="$(MSBuildSDKsPath)/../DotnetTools/dotnet-format/System.Composition*.dll"/></ItemGroup></Project>
```

Create `Program.cs`:

```csharp
using System;
using System.IO;
using System.Linq;
using Microsoft.CodeAnalysis;
using Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp;
using Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Syntax;
using Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Rename;
using Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Text;

using var workspace = new AdhocWorkspace();
var project = workspace.AddProject("Repro", LanguageNames.CSharp)
    .WithCompilationOptions(new CSharpCompilationOptions(OutputKind.DynamicallyLinkedLibrary))
    .WithParseOptions(new CSharpParseOptions(LanguageVersion.Preview))
    .AddMetadataReferences(((string)AppContext.GetData("TRUSTED_PLATFORM_ASSEMBLIES")).Split(Path.PathSeparator).Select(p => MetadataReference.CreateFromFile(p)));
var document = project.AddDocument("Logger.cs", SourceText.From(File.ReadAllText(args[0])));
var root = await document.GetSyntaxRootAsync();
var model = await document.GetSemanticModelAsync();
var parameter = root.DescendantNodes().OfType<ParameterSyntax>().Single(p => p.Identifier.ValueText == "messageFormatter");
var symbol = model.GetDeclaredSymbol(parameter);
Console.WriteLine(typeof(Renamer).Assembly.FullName);
var solution = await Renamer.RenameSymbolAsync(document.Project.Solution, symbol, new SymbolRenameOptions(), "formatter");
var renamed = solution.GetDocument(document.Id);
Console.WriteLine(await renamed.GetTextAsync());
var renamedRoot = await renamed.GetSyntaxRootAsync();
foreach (var node in renamedRoot.GetAnnotatedNodesAndTokens(Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CodeActions.ConflictAnnotation.Kind)) Console.WriteLine("CONFLICT: " + node);
var compilation = await renamed.Project.GetCompilationAsync();
foreach (var error in compilation.GetDiagnostics().Where(d => d.Severity == DiagnosticSeverity.Error)) Console.WriteLine(error);
```

Run `dotnet run --project Rename.csproj -- Logger.txt` with that SDK installation selected. The original source compiles. The output changes the method parameter and its invocation to `formatter`, but leaves `formatter.GetLogIssueCommand()` unchanged. Compilation of the returned solution reports:

```text
Logger.cs(17,37): error CS1061: 'Func<string>' does not contain a definition for 'GetLogIssueCommand'
```

No `CONFLICT:` annotations are printed.

**Diagnostic Id**: CS1061 after rename. This was first encountered by applying StyleCop.Analyzers 1.3.180's SA1315 code fix through `dotnet format`; the direct reproduction above isolates the rename API independently.

**Expected Behavior**:

Preserve the binding to the captured constructor parameter, or expose the unresolvable conflict so automated callers can decline the rename.

**Actual Behavior**:

`Renamer.RenameSymbolAsync` returns a solution whose existing constructor-parameter reference now binds to the method's delegate parameter, with a new compiler error and no conflict annotation.

Searches of open and closed issues for rename/primary-constructor, rename/shadow, and RenameSymbolAsync/constructor did not find this case. I inspected current main at `cb68799397aa13f795622b4aeb696baafb817da5`, including [declaration conflict detection](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/blob/cb68799397aa13f795622b4aeb696baafb817da5/src/Workspaces/CSharp/Portable/Rename/CSharpRenameRewriterLanguageService.cs#L807), rename local-conflict tests, unshipped workspace API notes, and the latest release notes; I found no documented correction. I have not built main, so this report claims reproduction on the released SDK only.

Please detect this captured primary-constructor binding conflict during rename.

Downstream tracking: ModularPipelines [#7464](https://github.com/thomhurst/ModularPipelines/issues/7464).

Issues.Title: Classify ERR_WrongArityAsyncReturn (CS8940) as a build-only diagnostic
Issues.Body:
Fixes #86391

`ERR_WrongArityAsyncReturn` (CS8940) is reported only while lowering an async method (`AsyncMethodBuilderMemberCollection.ValidateBuilderType`, reached from `AsyncRewriter`), so `SemanticModel.GetDiagnostics()` and `Compilation.GetDiagnostics()` never report it. `ErrorFacts.IsBuildOnlyDiagnostic` still returned `false` for it, and `CSharpLspBuildOnlyDiagnostics` did not list it. As a result, the IDE drops the error from the Error List after a build reports it.

This takes the minimal fix from the issue, option 2:
- `ErrorFacts.IsBuildOnlyDiagnostic` returns `true` for `ERR_WrongArityAsyncReturn`.
- `CSharpLspBuildOnlyDiagnostics` lists `CS8940`.
- `DiagnosticTest.TestIsBuildOnlyDiagnostic` expects it.
- `BuilderOnMethod_BoundGeneric_ReportedOnlyOnEmit` uses the repro from the issue. It checks that the compilation reports no diagnostics before emit and that emit reports CS8940.

Option 1 from the issue, reporting CS8940 while binding the `[AsyncMethodBuilder]` attribute, is left for a separate change, together with the other builder errors in #64314.

Issues.Title: Razor component binding can resolve a different type when names collide
Issues.Body:
Razor can bind a component from a referenced assembly, but the generated C# can resolve a different type with the same name in the current project.

For example, a referenced library contains a component:

```csharp
namespace Library;

public class Button : Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.ComponentBase { }
```

The app contains a different, non-component type with the same name:

```csharp
namespace Library;

public class Button { }
```

And an app component imports the library's namespace:

```razor
@using Library

<Button />
```

Razor finds the referenced component and generates:

```csharp
__builder.OpenComponent<global::Library.Button>(0);
```

C# resolves `global::Library.Button` to the app's type, so the generated code fails with `CS0311` because that type isn't a component. There can also be a `CS0436` warning about the conflicting types. `global::` identifies the root namespace, not an assembly.

With the component alias support in [dotnet/roslyn#86372](https://github.com/dotnet/roslyn/pull/86372), both of these have the same problem:

```razor
@using B = global::Library.Button

<B />
```

```razor
@using UI = global::Library

<UI.Button />
```

For the type alias, C# resolves `B` to the app's class, but Razor matches the library's component by name. The alias target map also compares equal when the alias changes from the library's component to the app's class, so incremental generation may not notice the change.

Razor shouldn't generate a component call that resolves to a different type from the one it bound.

I reproduced the three cases with the current compiler using a matching component descriptor. The ordinary-import path appears to predate the alias PR based on the old source, but I haven't run the example against the old compiler itself.

Issues.Title: Honor package source mapping in tool search and package completion
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Follow up on #55848 by applying package source mapping to tool search and package ID/version completion, so discovery results align with source selection when installing the tool or package.

- Filter tool search results by full package ID and originating source before expanding version details.
- Discover completion IDs on mapped enabled sources, then filter full returned IDs by origin rather than applying mapping to a partial stem. Preserve full-ID mapping for version completion.
- Honor explicit source overrides and reject additive-only sources when mapping is enabled.
- Pass selected project/file configuration context to completion, resolving relative sources against the invocation directory without MSBuild evaluation or project-count validation. Existing multi-project directories support completion; missing targets return no suggestions.
- Isolate completion source validation, resource discovery, and query failures per feed so healthy suggestions survive, while retaining HTTP opt-in requirements and default source validation for other callers.

Package acquisition, SDK installation, cache, signature policy, templates, and workload paths are unchanged. Completion uses directory-based NuGet configuration, not arbitrary MSBuild-evaluated restore properties. Defensive handling of versionless template catalog entries remains deferred.

## Validation

Windows x64:
- Managed CLI build passed with zero warnings/errors.
- 67 focused CLI tests, 7 source-configuration tests, and 5 actual NativeAOT tests passed, with no failures or skips.
- Native tests include concise/detailed managed/native tool-search parity over a controlled local feed.
- Regression coverage includes mapping precedence and origin filtering, overrides, HTTP opt-in and feed isolation, inherited configuration clearing, relative targets, and mid-line completion.
- Product/redist assembly hashes match; `git diff --check` passes.

Native product library increased by 1 KiB in the follow-up build; existing IL3053 dependency warnings remain, with no added suppressions. Linux/macOS and external authenticated-feed execution were not exercised.

Issues.Title: dotnetup: verify system root architecture from the dotnet executable header
Issues.Body:
## Problem

dotnetup decides a system root's architecture from where it was registered, not from what is on disk:

- **Windows:** the `HKLM\SOFTWARE\dotnet\Setup\InstalledVersions\{arch}` subkey that points at the folder ([`WindowsPathHelper.GetProgramFilesDotnetRoot`](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/release/dnup/src/Installer/dotnetup.Library/WindowsPathHelper.cs)).
- **macOS:** the `/etc/dotnet/install_location_{arch}` file, or the OS architecture for the arch-less file and default locations ([`DotnetEnvironmentManager.AddMacOSRoots`](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/blob/release/dnup/src/Installer/dotnetup.Library/DotnetEnvironmentManager.cs)).
- **Linux:** the OS architecture.

This matches how the .NET host finds its root, and it is correct for every layout the official installers produce. A registration that contradicts the files is still trusted, for example `InstalledVersions\x64\InstallLocation` pointing at an x86 install.

Before #56935, discovery loaded each root's `hostfxr`, and a mismatched root failed to load with `BadImageFormatException`, so it was skipped (with a warning). Discovery now walks folders without loading native code, so a mislabeled root is listed as dotnetup's own architecture.

## Impact

Low; nothing breaks:

- `dotnetup init` shows the folder as the system install location and labels its channels with dotnetup's architecture.
- Migration requests those channels for dotnetup's own root and architecture, so the user gets native builds; nothing is copied from the mislabeled folder.
- Layout conflict checks only look at dotnetup's own root and manifest, so there are no false conflicts.

The only failure would be a migrated channel with no build for dotnetup's architecture, which reports `NoMatchingReleaseFileForPlatform` and is classified as a Product error even though the machine is misconfigured.

## Proposal

Read the architecture from the root's `dotnet` executable header before trusting a root's label, and skip or warn when it does not match the expected architecture:

- **PE (`dotnet.exe`):** `MZ` header, `e_lfanew` at `0x3C`, `PE\0\0` signature, then the COFF `Machine` field: `0x14C` x86, `0x8664` x64, `0xAA64` arm64.
- **Mach-O / ELF:** the CPU type in the Mach-O header and `e_machine` in the ELF header.

This reads a few bytes and does not load or execute anything.

The VS Code .NET Install Tool already does this for PE, Mach-O, and ELF, and is a good starting point: [`ExecutableArchitectureDetector.ts`](https://github.com/dotnet/vscode-dotnet-runtime/blob/9c0a49f62da1b2d7190129c2e60e2dbe20aab2c9/vscode-dotnet-runtime-library/src/Utils/ExecutableArchitectureDetector.ts).

## Considerations

- A root can be partial and lack the muxer; keep the registration's label in that case.
- macOS universal binaries (fat Mach-O) need handling, or should keep the registration's label.
- The same check could apply to dotnetup's own roots and to `--architecture` support (#55083).
- Decide whether a mismatch is skipped silently, warned about, or recorded in telemetry.

Related: #56935, #55083, #55350.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue "dotnetup: verify system root architecture from the dotnet executable header" (#57075)

Issues.Title: Select issue triage assignees deterministically
Issues.Body:
## Summary

Issue triage has assigned every recent `Area-NuGet` issue to `@zivkan`. The prompt asked the agent to load-balance with `web-fetch`, but the Copilot CLI never exposes `web_fetch` to the model, even with `copilot-sdk: true`. The agent then fell back to "choose randomly" and picked the same name every time. In two runs, its reasoning named `@nkolev92` while the tool call assigned `@zivkan`.

This PR moves owner selection into code. A read-only `select-assignee` MCP script resolves the `CODEOWNERS` section, expands teams from a membership snapshot, counts each candidate's open issues created in the past week, and picks the lowest count. Ties are broken with `crypto.randomInt`. The agent calls the script once and assigns exactly the login it returns.

## Evidence

| dotnet/sdk run | Issue | Assigned |
|---|---|---|
| [42011849728](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/actions/runs/42011849728) | #56943 | zivkan |
| [42618174003](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/actions/runs/42618174003) | #57002 | zivkan |
| [43016080908](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/actions/runs/43016080908) | #57062 | zivkan |
| [43018542973](https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/actions/runs/43018542973) | #57063 | zivkan |

Each run's `agent` artifact (`sandbox/agent/logs/process-*.log`) shows that the model's tool list had no `web_fetch` and that the model reasoned it "can't fetch pages".

## Changes

- `.github/scripts/issue-triage-assignee.js`: selection logic. A pre-agent step copies it, its snapshot, and `CODEOWNERS` to `${{ runner.temp }}/issue-triage-private`, and a JavaScript `mcp-scripts` tool loads it from that copy. It uses the read-only `GITHUB_TOKEN` and reads only the issue search API; the area input is validated and never interpolated into a query.
- `.github/scripts/issue-triage-team-snapshot.json`: team snapshot moved out of the prompt, unchanged.
- `issue-triage.md`: removes `web-fetch:` and `copilot-sdk: true`, allows `mcpscripts:*`, and replaces the CODEOWNERS matching and load-balancing instructions with "call `select_assignee` and use its result". The lock file was regenerated with gh-aw v1.0.1 on Linux.
- `.github/scripts/issue-triage-assignee.test.js`: unit tests, run by the existing helper-tests workflow. One test checks that every CODEOWNERS and snapshot team is listed in `safe-outputs.mentions.allowed`.

## Security

- **Token scope.** The tool receives the agent job's `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which has `contents: read` and `issues: read`. The workflow already passes the same token to the MCP gateway, the GitHub CLI proxy, and safe outputs. Only the host-side MCP scripts server receives it; the agent sandbox does not. The agent can already make the same reads through `gh`.
- **No agent-writable code.** The agent sandbox mounts the workspace read-write and has the `write` tool. Loading the selector from the checkout would therefore let a prompt-injected agent rewrite it and run code on the runner host. The selector and its inputs are staged under `runner.temp`, which the sandbox does not mount, before the agent starts. `stale-reference-interpret.md` uses the same pattern. The tool is a JavaScript handler, not a `run:` handler: a `run:` handler would resolve `node` through `PATH`, which includes the agent-writable `~/.local/bin`.
- **Regression tests.** Tests check that staging runs after checkout and before the agent, and that the tool never references `GITHUB_WORKSPACE`.

## Behavior changes to review

- **ILLink/ReadyToRun section boundary.** The old prompt's rule ("stop at the next comment") contradicted its own ILLink example, which included `@dotnet/dotnet-cli` below an in-section comment. A section now ends at a comment that follows a blank line, or at the next `Area-*` heading. This matches the example.
- **Load metric.** The count no longer filters on `label:untriaged`. Triage removes that label when it assigns someone, so the old query counted roughly zero for everyone.
- **No assignability preflight.** The old prompt mentioned one but never defined it. Stale snapshot members will fail at assignment, as they do today.

## Validation

- `node --test .github/scripts/agentic-workflow-guards.test.js .github/scripts/issue-triage-assignee.test.js .github/stale-reference-check/test/*.test.mjs` passes.
- A 2000-trial test confirms that every candidate with equal load is selected at a near-uniform rate.
- I ran the branch in `nagilson/sdk` against verbatim copies of three NuGet issues. Each run picked a different person, and the agent assigned exactly the script's choice. On the fork the assignment itself is not applied, because these users are not collaborators there.

| Fork run | Copy of | Script choice | `assign_to_user` |
|---|---|---|---|
| [43106795411](https://github.com/nagilson/sdk/actions/runs/43106795411) | #56943 | jebriede | jebriede |
| [43107739780](https://github.com/nagilson/sdk/actions/runs/43107739780) | #57063 | kartheekp-ms | kartheekp-ms |
| [43107744271](https://github.com/nagilson/sdk/actions/runs/43107744271) | #57062 | nkolev92 | nkolev92 |
| [43126774449](https://github.com/nagilson/sdk/actions/runs/43126774449) (staged loader) | #56943 | martinrrm | martinrrm |

Issues.Title: Enable optimized Native AOT publish by default
Issues.Body:
🤖 The optimized Native AOT publish path was made opt-in for .NET 11 to reduce rollout risk, and that release-branch change flowed into `main`. With `main` now targeting .NET 12, restore the optimization as the default while preserving an explicit compatibility opt-out.

- Default `UseOptimizedPublish` to `true` for Native AOT publish.
- Keep `UseOptimizedPublish=false` and `NoBuild` behavior covered by the existing test matrix.
- Make the project-reference scenario exercise the default optimized path.
- Document the different .NET 11 and .NET 12 defaults.

- `build.cmd`
- `Microsoft.NET.Publish.Tests`: `NativeAot_publish_respects_optimized_publish_and_no_build` and `NativeAot_publish_with_project_reference_succeeds` (7 passed)

Issues.Title: [release/10.0.4xx] Fix native MTP target framework and runtime display
Issues.Body:
## Description

Backport of #57035 (merge commit `0a0943c49529c7902ce706d6fc713310f0644728`) to `release/10.0.4xx`.

Relates to microsoft/testfx#7066.

Separate a test module's actual target framework from its executing runtime. Project/solution runs prefer the evaluated `TargetFramework`; module-only runs can use optional handshake field 21; otherwise the target remains unknown. Required field 2 remains runtime information, with this branch's existing protocol 1.0 and required-field behavior unchanged.

This is a release-branch adaptation, not a wholesale cherry-pick: retain the older reporter, xUnit tests, constructor/call signatures, retry accounting and summary behavior. Add a required sixth-argument runtime overload rather than importing newer attempt/settings APIs. Preserve identity through start, results, completion, discovery, summary and both progress renderers; narrow cursor progress drops secondary runtime information before target/architecture or the filename. The new field is also named `TargetFramework` in existing handshake traces.

The controller-capability post-processing correction from the source PR is inapplicable because `ArtifactPostProcessingManager` does not exist here. No newer heartbeat, error-recap, post-processing, retry/settings or test-framework infrastructure is imported. This branch has no vendored-files manifest; the shared formatter is attributed to the immutable TestFX source commit instead. All 13 XLF updates were generated with `UpdateXlf`.

## Customer Impact

A genuine `net472` test running on .NET Framework 4.8.1 now displays `(net472|x64, runtime: net481)`, rather than falsely identifying its target as `(net481|x64)`. A known matching target stays compact, for example `(net481|x64)`. An older module-only peer without target metadata displays `(x64, runtime: net481)` without inferring a target from the runtime or output directory.

Full target TFMs and platform suffixes remain visible. Modern runtime servicing patches and target platform suffixes are ignored only when comparing target/runtime equality; .NET Framework `net48`/`net481` and `net471`/`net472` remain distinct. The architecture is the actual executing process architecture.

## Regression?

The introduction commit has not been established. The untouched release-branch base `3d90ce145149e0369f594f1289f27528c98d2f21` reproduces the incorrect identity in the branch-built SDK, including passing, failing and zero-result runs. This PR does not attribute the bug to a particular introducing change.

## Risk

Low code risk: limited to identity metadata and presentation, with no selection, result-count, command, exit-code or dependency-policy changes. The corrected module-only output for old peers is an intentional user-visible change and may affect consumers parsing the previous incorrect identity.

Branch dependencies remain unchanged and coherent: `Microsoft.Testing.Platform` **2.1.0-preview.25571.1** and `MSTest` **4.1.0-preview.25571.1**, both from TestFX `43e592148ac1c7916908477bdffcf2a345affa6d`. Optional target metadata from a newer peer is not required for project/solution correctness or old-peer compatibility.

The default full build has an independently reproduced baseline blocker: installer `finalizer.csproj` restores `Microsoft.DotNet.ILCompiler` 10.0.12 and fails with **NU1903**, https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p3jp-9v83-76w9. Managed redist and CLI/test builds passed. Native-AOT finalizer/installer validation is not claimed; no audit/analyzer diagnostics were suppressed and no package versions were changed. Servicing approval is not claimed.

## Testing

**73/73 focused xUnit tests passed**, with zero failures, errors or skips, against the committed source. Coverage includes formatter comparison, old/new/absent metadata, required runtime fields, controller-before-host ordering, stable retry identity/counts, cursor widths/long filenames, simple progress, discovery/summary surfaces, real project/glob runs, legacy retry and no-handshake failures.

**25/25 composed product cases passed** using the branch-built **10.0.403** shipping SDK layout: **14** new-peer cases and **11** cases with the unchanged 2.1 peer. These are real MTP executions, not helper mocks or an installed newer CLI. Each run uses an explicit isolated consumer CWD, SDK/root/resolver settings and separate package caches. Parent exit codes and summary counts are checked against independently generated target/runtime/process/selected/executed/outcome XML; multi-module runs also verify both artifacts and aggregate counts.

| Observable path | Verified result |
|---|---|
| `net472` project, old/new peer | `(net472|x64, runtime: net481)`; exit 0, selected/executed/passed 1 |
| `net472` module, new peer | `(net472|x64, runtime: net481)`; exit 0, executed/passed 1 |
| `net472` module, old peer | `(x64, runtime: net481)`; exit 0, executed/passed 1 |
| Known matching `net481` and `net10.0` targets | Compact target/architecture identity; exit 0 |
| `net8.0` major roll-forward | Target remains `net8.0`, runtime is `net10.0`; actual runtime .NET 10.0.12 |
| Genuinely absent assembly target metadata | Module target unknown; evaluated project target still preferred |
| Actual x86 .NET Framework process | `(net472|x86, runtime: net481)`; XML confirms X86 and one passed test |
| Deliberate failure, old/new peer | Exit 2; selected/executed/failed 1; failure diagnostic preserved |
| Zero-result run, old/new peer | Exit 8; selected/executed/total 0 |
| `net472` + `net481`, old/new peer | Exit 0; two independent execution artifacts; total/succeeded 2 |

Five additional **clean-base red-phase** cases retain the original incorrect identity with independently verified exits/outcomes; the matching `net481` control stays compact. They are source-built evidence, not the separate installed-SDK baseline.

The new-peer test package `Microsoft.Testing.Platform.3.0.0-dev.framework7066.final1` was used only in an isolated local feed/cache. Its nuspec source stamp is `c2b618b17ef3ecbf46054cde3785476673ff9f63` and SHA-256 is `E476C77337E7AF644D03D475F36DCECFE8307CB66BB36058316F6BA6FCAF8139`; it is not a shipping dependency upgrade. Existing traces explicitly retain `Framework: .NET Framework 4.8.10008.0` and `TargetFramework: net472`.

Build/test commands (PowerShell; binary logs retained):

```powershell
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe build src\Layout\redist\redist.csproj -c Debug -m -p:PublishAot=false -p:SkipBuildingInstallers=true -p:SkipUsingCrossgen=true -bl:baseline-managed-layout.binlog --nologo -v:minimal
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe msbuild src\Cli\dotnet\dotnet.csproj -t:UpdateXlf -p:Configuration=Debug -bl:localization.binlog -nologo -v:minimal
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe build test\dotnet.Tests\dotnet.Tests.csproj -c Debug --no-restore -m -p:PublishAot=false -bl:commit-stamped-build.binlog --nologo -v:minimal
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe exec artifacts\bin\redist\Debug\dotnet.Tests.dll -method '*TestFrameworkDisplayTests.*' -method '*TerminalTestReporterTests.*' -method '*TestApplicationHandlerTests.*' -method '*TestProgressStateTests.*' -method '*GivenDotnetTestReportsTargetFramework.*' -method '*GivenDotnetTestBuildsAndRunsTestBasedOnGlobbingFilter.*' -method '*GivenDotnetTestRunsConsoleAppWithoutHandshake.*' -method '*RunTestProjectWithWithRetryFeature_ShouldSucceed*' -xml commit-tests.xml -nologo
```

The committed CLI and its 13 existing satellite assemblies were deployed into `artifacts\bin\redist\Debug\dotnet\sdk\10.0.403` before the final test and composed-product runs. The source map identifies the exact commit below.

<details>
<summary>Retained result/provenance manifest</summary>

```json
{
  "commit": "a75067deadfb8e11faaefa2b7af1545f66f5cbce",
  "parent": "3d90ce145149e0369f594f1289f27528c98d2f21",
  "sdk": "10.0.403",
  "baselineCliSha256": "37D66A9D2EB183385E2DAAB8072EBF5AD686819D2ABA2A21A1218C48175BC5E6",
  "testedCliSha256": "D7BD3987EC20F8EFB8AA35C88DA423A10EC0CECB0E6BFB1F07AF70604621350C",
  "focusedTests": { "total": 73, "passed": 73, "failed": 0, "skipped": 0 },
  "composedCases": { "newPeer": 14, "shippingPeer": 11, "cleanBaseRed": 5 },
  "generatedXlfFiles": 13,
  "nativeFinalizerValidated": false,
  "diagnosticsSuppressed": false
}
```

Full evidence retains the xUnit XML/log, per-case stdout/stderr/commands/traces and independently emitted execution XML, old/new/baseline summaries, package hashes/source stamps, source map and build/localization binlogs.

</details>

Issues.Title: [release/11.0.1xx] Fix native MTP target framework and runtime display
Issues.Body:
### Description

Backport of #57035 to `release/11.0.1xx` (source merge `0a0943c49529c7902ce706d6fc713310f0644728`).

Keep the test assembly's target framework separate from its executing runtime. Prefer the evaluated project TFM, then genuine optional handshake `TargetFramework` metadata (field 21); keep required `Framework` field 2 as runtime information. Matching runs remain compact, while a mismatch is explicit:

```text
tests.exe (net472|x64, runtime: net481)
tests.exe (net481|x64)
```

Missing module-only target metadata stays unknown, for example `(x64, runtime: net481)`. Keep the established identity across retries and the branch's existing start, result, completion, summary and progress surfaces. Include the review correction that fills a missing post-processing target when a later host handshake arrives, even if it does not repeat the controller's capabilities; preserve known targets, capability sets and the existing lock.

This is a manual adaptation after the repository backport workflow encountered conflicts. It does not import main's newer heartbeat, errored-assembly recap, per-application settings, retry or post-processing features. Legacy public reporter overloads are preserved. The relevant shared-source baselines remain TestFx-owned and use exact blobs from `c2b618b17ef3ecbf46054cde3785476673ff9f63`; unrelated baselines are unchanged. Related localization files were regenerated through `UpdateXlf`.

Relates to microsoft/testfx#7066. This release backport does not close the upstream issue.

### Customer Impact

Native MTP `dotnet test` can misidentify which target ran, notably reporting a `net472` application on .NET Framework 4.8.1 as `(net481|x64)`. This affects diagnostic accuracy in local and CI logs when the target and executing runtime differ, including modern .NET major-version roll-forward. The problem was reproduced in .NET SDK 11.0.100 and on the unmodified `release/11.0.1xx` source build.

The fix reports target/process identity without changing test execution or pass/fail policy. Existing MTP packages work for project runs without an upgrade. Legacy module-only peers that cannot supply a genuine target now explicitly report the runtime rather than inventing a target.

### Regression?

Unknown. The introducing change has not been identified. On the untouched branch base `2b2b3b81a48ded73d2583c6eb1682ab6a5eb8790`, a real `net472` test executed and passed with exit 0, but its start, result and completion all incorrectly displayed `net481|x64`.

### Risk

Low. The change is limited to MTP identity formatting and target metadata, with focused protocol, lifecycle, reporter and integration coverage. Optional field 21 is additive; existing required-field validation, supported protocol versions, retry behavior and exit-code policies are preserved. The late capability-state correction fills only a missing target under the existing lock.

The backport retains this branch's reporter APIs and multi-module summary behavior instead of importing newer main-only features. No package upgrade is included: shipping MTP remains `3.0.0-preview.26556.8`, and MSTest/MSTest.Sdk remain the coherent `5.0.0-preview.26556.8` build. No .NET 10 changes are included.

### Testing

Local validation against the actual release11 shipping layout, not main's validation results:

- Full clean-base SDK build and patched managed CLI build/deployment succeeded. The unchanged branch reproduced the bug before the patch.
- **212 focused tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped**, covering target/runtime precedence, required and optional handshake metadata, late controller capabilities, legacy/retry compatibility, ANSI/non-ANSI rendering, module globbing, roll-forward and multi-target integration. Cursor-renderer checks cover widths 40, 80 and 120.
- **25 actual composed-product scenarios passed** with built SDK `11.0.100-dev`: 14 with the new producer and 11 with the branch-pinned legacy peer. These exercise project/module `net472` mismatch, matching `net481` and `net11.0`, `net8.0` rolling forward to .NET 11, genuinely missing target metadata, actual x86 execution and two-module aggregation. Independent execution XML verifies target attributes, runtime, process architecture and selected/executed/result counts. Deliberate failure remains exit **2** with one failed test; zero results remain exit **8** with zero executed tests.
- The new peer uses the separate local `Microsoft.Testing.Platform` package `3.0.0-dev.framework7066.final1` from TestFx `c2b618b17ef3ecbf46054cde3785476673ff9f63` (SHA256 `E476C77337E7AF644D03D475F36DCECFE8307CB66BB36058316F6BA6FCAF8139`), without changing shipping dependencies. Both result sets verify the final CLI SHA256 `826FCA0C94132537F52751A53D08E899251360D2D0381FD0D1FF24687563FD98`; all 13 deployed satellite assemblies match their built outputs.
- Vendoring manifest validation, append-only source-index checks, generated localization checks and `git diff --check` passed.

Reproducible focused-test command from the repository root:

```powershell
.\.dotnet\dotnet.exe .github\skills\targeted-test\scripts\RunTargetedTests.cs -- --project test\dotnet.Tests\dotnet.Tests.csproj --filter 'FullyQualifiedName~TestApplicationHandlerTests|FullyQualifiedName~ArtifactPostProcessingManagerTests|FullyQualifiedName~TerminalTestReporterTests|FullyQualifiedName~TestFrameworkDisplayTests|FullyQualifiedName~GivenDotnetTestReportsTargetFramework|FullyQualifiedName~GivenDotnetTestBuildsAndRunsTestBasedOnGlobbingFilter'
```

The composed probe ran each peer against `artifacts\bin\redist\Debug\dotnet`, with explicit consumer working-directory/SDK selection and separate package caches. Final TRX, build binlogs, per-case commands/logs and independent execution XML are retained.

Existing audit findings were **not suppressed or changed**: MessagePack `3.1.8` (`NU1902`) and System.Security.Cryptography.Pkcs `8.0.1` (`NU1902`/`NU1903`). The baseline build succeeded with 12 existing warnings; focused test builds retain the MessagePack warning. These are unrelated dependency findings, not new backport regressions.

Issues.Title: .NET SDK 11.0.100 Static Web Assets net472 tasks ship an incompatible Microsoft.Bcl.AsyncInterfaces version
Issues.Body: ### Describe the bug When a `Microsoft.NET.Sdk.Web` project is built with .NET SDK 11.0.100 using full-framework Visual Studio MSBuild, the Static Web Assets task fails to load `Microsoft.Bcl.AsyncInterfaces, Version=10.0.0.10`. The same project builds with core-hosted MSBuild (`dotnet build`). ### Steps to reproduce Install .NET SDK 11.0.100 and use a Visual Studio Developer Command Prompt whose full-framework MSBuild supports that SDK. global.json: ```json { "sdk": { "version": "11.0.100", "rollForward": "disable" } } ``` Repro.csproj: ```xml net11.0 enable ``` Program.cs: ```cs var builder = WebApplication.CreateBuilder(args); var app = builder.Build(); app.MapGet("/", () => "Hello"); app.Run(); ``` From that directory, verify dotnet --version reports 11.0.100, then run: ```ps1 msbuild Repro.csproj /restore /v:minimal ``` ### Expected behavior The project builds successfully, as it does with: ``` dotnet build Repro.csproj ``` ### Actual behavior Full-framework MSBuild fails in Microsoft.NET.Sdk.StaticWebAssets.targets while generating the Static Web Assets manifest: ``` error : FileNotFoundException: Could not load file or assembly 'Microsoft.Bcl.AsyncInterfaces, Version=10.0.0.10, Culture=neutral, PublicKeyToken=cc7b13ffcd2ddd51' or one of its dependencies. at Microsoft.AspNetCore.StaticWebAssets.Tasks.StaticWebAssetsManifest.ComputeManifestHash() ``` Another observed path throws during initialization of `StaticWebAssetEndpointResponseHeader` through `StaticWebAssetsJsonSerializerContext`. ### Is this a regression? Yes. Our builds were fine under .NET SDK 10.0.402 ### Are there any workarounds? Copilot came up with a couple different workarounds: #### Surgical assembly resolver ```xml { var requestedAssembly = new AssemblyName(args.Name); if (requestedAssembly.Name == "Microsoft.Bcl.AsyncInterfaces" && requestedAssembly.Version == new Version(10, 0, 0, 10)) { return Assembly.LoadFrom(AssemblyPath); } return null; }; ]]> <_StaticWebAssetsBclAsyncInterfacesAssembly>$([System.IO.Path]::GetFullPath('$(StaticWebAssetsSdkDirectoryRoot)\..\..\DotnetTools\dotnet-format\BuildHost-net472\Microsoft.Bcl.AsyncInterfaces.dll')) ``` #### A bunch of UsingTask elements ```xml <_StaticWebAssetsNetTasksAssembly>$(NetCoreRoot)sdk\$(NETCoreSdkVersion)\Sdks\Microsoft.NET.Sdk.StaticWebAssets\tasks\net472\Microsoft.NET.Sdk.StaticWebAssets.Tasks.dll ``` ### dotnet --info output ```console ``` ### IDE version _No response_ ### Other details **Payload analysis** For full-framework MSBuild, `Sdk.StaticWebAssets.CurrentVersion.targets` selects the tasks/net472 task payload. In SDK 11.0.100 that directory contains: * `System.Text.Json.dll` assembly version 10.0.0.10, which references `Microsoft.Bcl.AsyncInterfaces` version 10.0.0.10. * Microsoft.Bcl.AsyncInterfaces.dll assembly version 11.0.0.0. * No Microsoft.Bcl.AsyncInterfaces version 10.0.0.10 and no binding redirect for it. Because this is a strong-named dependency loaded by .NET Framework MSBuild, version 11.0.0.0 does not satisfy the request for 10.0.0.10. Interestingly, the SDK contains the required 10.0.0.10 assembly elsewhere at `DotnetTools/dotnet-format/BuildHost-net472/Microsoft.Bcl.AsyncInterfaces.dll`; copying/resolving that assembly makes the task run. The tasks/net472 directory should ship a consistent dependency closure, for example by including Microsoft.Bcl.AsyncInterfaces 10.0.0.10 or by rebuilding/shipping dependencies that consistently reference version 11.
Issues.RelatedDescription: Open issue ".NET SDK 11.0.100 Static Web Assets net472 tasks ship an incompatible Microsoft.Bcl.AsyncInterfaces version" (#57068)

Issues.Title: dotnet nuget never exits when run as PID 1 on first use (no first-use sentinel)
Issues.Body:
### Describe the bug

When dotnet runs as PID 1 and the first-use sentinel (`~/.dotnet/<version>.dotnetFirstUseSentinel`) does not exist yet, `dotnet nuget` commands never exit. The command does its work and prints its output, but the process stays alive forever.

It only happens when both conditions hold:
• dotnet is PID 1. With `docker run --init`, or with dotnet started as a normal child process, it works.
• First-use setup has not run yet. If the sentinel files exist, or any earlier `dotnet nuget` call ran as a normal child process, it works.

Real-world impact: 
docker build hangs indefinitely on a step like RUN dotnet nuget update source ... when the base image hasn't run first-use setup. Docker runs a single-command RUN as /bin/sh -c "...", and the shell hands PID 1 to dotnet. It happens both locally and in CI. This was not the case in .NET 10



### Steps to reproduce

docker run -d --name hang -e HOME=/tmp --entrypoint dotnet mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:11.0@sha256:65f3c7c6a25a239ab3e6719f2896147e7b68242ff2d8818dd70498bde6ef8bea nuget list source

sleep 10; 
docker logs hang; 
docker inspect -f '{{.State.Running}}' hang   # output printed, still running
docker rm -f hang

### Expected behavior

The command exits with the NuGet child's exit code, as it does when dotnet isn't PID 1 

### Actual behavior

The command prints its output and then hangs until it's killed

### Is this a regression?

Yes, we've only picked up this issue after upgrading from .NET 10 to .NET 11

### Are there any workarounds?

Yes, by using `timeout` like this:

`RUN timeout 60s dotnet nuget update source "github" ....`

instead of:
`RUN dotnet nuget update source "github"....`

Issues.Title: Fix dotnet-watch temporary solution sharing on Windows
Issues.Body:
`ServerAndResources` hung because dotnet-watch retained write access to its generated `.slnx`, preventing MSBuild from opening it on Windows.

- **File lifecycle**
  - Close the write handle after generating the solution.
  - Reopen it read-only while MSBuild consumes it, preserving protection from modification.

- **Regression coverage**
  - Verify concurrent readers are allowed while write access remains denied.

The dossier establishes recurrence of this work-item mechanism in the current and 1674681 builds; it does not establish that every intervening build failed for the same mechanism.

Exact current observation excerpt:
`Test host crashed; recovered 93 test result(s) from the TRX streaming sidecar (additional results that were in flight at crash time may be missing). Test application process didn\u0027t exit gracefully, exit code is \u0027-1\u0027 [00:50:52] ServerAndResources`

The Helix work item reported exit code `7`; 89 tests passed and 93 results were recovered. Console: [console.e009ed57.log](https://helix.dot.net/api/jobs/4cfe0716-7bcd-4343-a833-8bda31691a07/workitems/dotnet-watch.Tests.dll.1/files/console.e009ed57.log?api-version=2019-06-17). Dump artifacts: [dotnet\_9384\_hang.dmp](https://helix.dot.net/api/jobs/4cfe0716-7bcd-4343-a833-8bda31691a07/workitems/dotnet-watch.Tests.dll.1/files/dotnet_9384_hang.dmp?api-version=2019-06-17), [WatchAspire\_1788\_hang.dmp](https://helix.dot.net/api/jobs/4cfe0716-7bcd-4343-a833-8bda31691a07/workitems/dotnet-watch.Tests.dll.1/files/Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire_1788_hang.dmp?api-version=2019-06-17), [WatchAspire\_4324\_hang.dmp](https://helix.dot.net/api/jobs/4cfe0716-7bcd-4343-a833-8bda31691a07/workitems/dotnet-watch.Tests.dll.1/files/Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire_4324_hang.dmp?api-version=2019-06-17), [WatchAspire\_6520\_hang.dmp](https://helix.dot.net/api/jobs/4cfe0716-7bcd-4343-a833-8bda31691a07/workitems/dotnet-watch.Tests.dll.1/files/Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire_6520_hang.dmp?api-version=2019-06-17).

- **Observed:** The test application did not exit gracefully while `ServerAndResources` was active; the test host crashed, dump files were written, and the TRX sidecar recovered results.
- **Assessment:** The immediate cause of the work-item failure is an abnormal test-host/application termination during test execution. The dossier does not establish why the process terminated; the generic `Monitor Helix Jobs` failure is a downstream parent, not the cause.
- **Confidence:** Medium for the immediate crash mechanism; Low for the underlying cause. Recurrence is supported by two independent main-branch builds, but recurrence alone does not establish flakiness or the crash trigger.
- **Alternatives / Unknowns:** The dumps and logs have not been analyzed, so a product deadlock, test-host/runtime failure, resource issue, or environment-specific condition remain possible.

2. Inspect the corresponding `dotnet-watch` test and recent build progression/changed files to determine whether a code change correlates with the recurrence.

Issues.Title: Bound external registry manifest test duration
Issues.Body:
`CanReadManifestFromRegistry` could remain blocked on an unresponsive external registry until Helix terminated the test host after 48 minutes.

- **Bound registry requests**
  - Add a two-minute deadline to the manifest probe.
  - Link it to MSTest cancellation so either deadline stops the request.

```csharp
using CancellationTokenSource timeout =
    CancellationTokenSource.CreateLinkedTokenSource(TestContext.CancellationToken);
timeout.CancelAfter(TimeSpan.FromMinutes(2));
```

## Failure History

The current build is the first supplied occurrence of this exact actionable fingerprint, with one occurrence. The five related main-branch builds were failed for different supplied mechanisms and do not establish recurrence. No matching pass or fail sequence is available in the dossier.

## Error Details

Exact excerpt: Hang dump timeout of 00:48:00 expired; The following tests were still running when dump was taken; Test host crashed; recovered 13 test result(s) from the TRX streaming sidecar; Test application process did not exit gracefully, exit code is 137; \[00:48:01\] CanReadManifestFromRegistry (registry.access.redhat.com/ubi8/dotnet-70).
The Helix work item exit code was 7. Recovered TRX summary: 13 executed and 13 passed, with no failed, error, timeout, or aborted results. Console: [https://helix.dot.net/api/jobs/a8b82899-2713-4ec7-a3d3-781ddc69b075/workitems/Microsoft.NET.Build.Containers.IntegrationTests.dll.2/files/console.5f17fa37.log?api-version=2019-06-17](https://helix.dot.net/api/jobs/a8b82899-2713-4ec7-a3d3-781ddc69b075/workitems/Microsoft.NET.Build.Containers.IntegrationTests.dll.2/files/console.5f17fa37.log?api-version=2019-06-17)
Dump: [https://helix.dot.net/api/jobs/a8b82899-2713-4ec7-a3d3-781ddc69b075/workitems/Microsoft.NET.Build.Containers.IntegrationTests.dll.2/files/dotnet\_3143\_hang.dmp?api-version=2019-06-17](https://helix.dot.net/api/jobs/a8b82899-2713-4ec7-a3d3-781ddc69b075/workitems/Microsoft.NET.Build.Containers.IntegrationTests.dll.2/files/dotnet_3143_hang.dmp?api-version=2019-06-17)
