## Root Cause Analysis

- **Observed:** The test host remained active for 48 minutes while CanReadManifestFromRegistry was active. Helix captured a hang dump, the host did not exit gracefully, and the process exited with code 137; the monitor then reported the work-item failure.
- **Assessment:** The proximate cause is the integration-test host timeout and abnormal termination. The underlying reason the registry manifest operation did not complete is not established by the dossier.
- **Confidence:** Medium for the timeout and termination chain; Low for the underlying hang cause.
- **Alternatives / Unknowns:** A registry or service response stall, container or runtime interaction, machine resource pressure, or test-host deadlock could produce this hang. The dossier does not establish which occurred, and does not establish that the failure is flaky or PR-related.

## Suggested Investigation

1. Inspect the hang dump and full console log to identify the blocked thread and registry or container subprocess state.
2. Compare the test and container-registry changes on the target branch and inspect the timeout and cancellation path.
3. Correlate the run with registry availability and machine resource telemetry; a rerun is diagnostic only and does not prove root cause.

The generic Monitor Helix Jobs parent failure and artifact or result cascades are consequences of this work-item failure, not separate causes.

Issues.Title: Reduce CA1851 and shared dataflow analysis overhead
Issues.Body:
> [!NOTE]
> Drafted with AI assistance.

## Summary

Reduce CA1851 and shared dataflow-analysis overhead by avoiding unnecessary analysis and repeated tracking, lookup, and reporting work.

- Add conservative CA1851 source pre-analysis, bound repeated deferred-path expansion, and share enumeration-reporting state.
- Index operation and child-entity lookups, group argument postprocessing by parent, reuse unchanged abstract values, and remove redundant taint discovery and formatting.
- Make CFG/result caches compilation-owned, preserve canonical live CFG identity, and include supported-type and mapping policies in cache keys without retaining pooled callback state.
- Correct entity/location/index equality and normalize named-indexer keys by bound parameter order while preserving argument evaluation order.

Rule IDs, defaults, and severities are unchanged.

## Performance

Focused synthetic workloads, comparing preserved pre-optimization component baselines with the final Release implementation; compiler binding is excluded. The CA1851 baseline already includes the original narrow one-direct-input shortcut.

| Workload | Elapsed time, before -> after | Managed allocation, before -> after |
|---|---|---|
| 256 once-used enumerable aliases | 55-56 -> 7.6 ms (**86% less**) | 7.43 -> 2.85 MB (**62% less**) |
| 256 once-used LINQ pipelines | 146-151 -> 46-48 ms (**69% less**) | 32.86 -> 16.12 MB (**51% less**) |
| 256 inputs, eight enumerations each: 2,048 sites | 1.50-1.58 s -> 85-89 ms (**94% less**) | 43.48 -> 26.84 MB (**38% less**) |
| Shared flow: 1,024 locals, 256 uncertain-index writes | 61-65 -> 36 ms (**42% less**) | 14.64 -> 5.29 MB (**64% less**) |

Times are ranges of run medians from baseline/final ABBA comparisons, with three warmups and seven CA1851 or twelve shared-flow measured samples per run. Allocation figures are rounded means of the two per-run medians; MB denotes decimal megabytes.

These are component-level results, **not end-to-end project-build or peak-memory savings**. Smaller and mixed-analyzer workloads were not uniformly faster.

Issues.Title: Allow extending metadata preserved by GetCopyToPublishDirectoryItems
Issues.Body:
`GetCopyToPublishDirectoryItems` drops metadata outside a fixed allowlist, preventing downstream SDKs from consuming custom metadata from local or referenced-project items.

- **Extensibility**
  - Adds `MSBuildGetCopyToPublishDirectoryAdditionalItemMetadataToCopy`.
  - Appends its semicolon-separated values to the optimized metadata allowlist.

- **Behavior**
  - Preserves requested metadata for current and referenced projects.
  - Retains existing filtering when the property is unset.

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <MSBuildGetCopyToPublishDirectoryAdditionalItemMetadataToCopy>
    $(MSBuildGetCopyToPublishDirectoryAdditionalItemMetadataToCopy);PublishFolderType
  </MSBuildGetCopyToPublishDirectoryAdditionalItemMetadataToCopy>
</PropertyGroup>
```

The property must be configured in every project where publish-item filtering occurs.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->

- Fixes #57024

Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-118740 - Aspire Security Feature Bypass Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Aspire. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. Aspire Dashboard's unauthenticated NotFound route can permit telemetry deletion in both standalone and AppHost-hosted deployments. In standalone deployments using browser-token authentication, it can also expose the browser token. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/aspire/issues/22148 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Critical - **Score:** 9.1 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N` - **Weakness:** CWE-862 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Any supported OS - **Architectures:** x64, Arm64 ## Affected Packages ### Standalone Aspire Dashboard Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- Aspire Dashboard | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 Both 13.6.3 and 13.6.4 contain the unauthenticated NotFound route. ### Aspire Dashboard SDK packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-arm64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-musl-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.linux-musl-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.osx-arm64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-x64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk.win-arm64) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Aspire Dashboard releases through 13.6.4 are affected, whether deployed independently or launched by an Aspire AppHost. For an AppHost using Dashboard SDK packages, check the resolved Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk package versions against the affected ranges above. If the AppHost selects a CLI-bundled Dashboard or a custom Dashboard path, check the version of that Dashboard instead. Aspire ships independently of .NET; installing a .NET runtime or SDK update does not replace the Dashboard. ### How do I fix the issue? Update Aspire Dashboard to version 13.6.5 or later. Neither 13.6.3 nor 13.6.4 is a fixed upgrade target. For container deployments, explicitly set the Dashboard image to `mcr.microsoft.com/aspire/dashboard:13.6.5` and recreate or redeploy the container. Replace older version tags and nightly image references, including those in generated Docker Compose or Kubernetes manifests, with this fixed stable image. Updating AppHost package references alone does not replace an image reference in an existing deployment manifest. For an AppHost using Dashboard SDK packages, update any explicit Aspire.Hosting.AppHost version, including a central package version, to 13.6.5 or later. If that reference is supplied implicitly by Aspire.AppHost.Sdk, update the SDK reference to 13.6.5 or later instead. Restore and rebuild the AppHost, verify that its resolved Aspire.Dashboard.Sdk packages are 13.6.5 or later, and restart the AppHost to run the updated Dashboard. If your AppHost selects a CLI-bundled Dashboard or a custom Dashboard path, update the Dashboard in that selected bundle or location to 13.6.5 or later and restart the AppHost. Updating AppHost package references alone does not replace that Dashboard. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue in the Aspire repository at https://github.com/microsoft/aspire. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in ASP.NET Core. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. ASP.NET Core Identity scaffolding templates use the request-supplied email instead of the account's stored email for password-reset and confirmation messages. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/Scaffolding/issues/3959 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 8.1 (base score) - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-640 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Any supported OS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages Updating scaffolding packages/tools does not repair previously generated application code. Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc contains the affected templates. Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design is a parent package that brings in the MVC generator through a minimum-version dependency. For Design, applicability depends on the resolved MVC generator: a project that independently resolves a fixed MVC version does not become vulnerable merely because it retains an older Design reference. ### 8.0 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.23 | 8.0.24 [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design) | >= 8.0.0, <= 8.0.23 | 8.0.24 ### 9.0 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.12 | 9.0.13 [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design) | >= 9.0.0, <= 9.0.12 | 9.0.13 ### 10.0 - standalone packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.2 | 10.0.3 [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design) | >= 10.0.0, <= 10.0.2 | 10.0.3 ### Additional known affected scaffolding prereleases These are exact known affected versions, not continuous prerelease intervals. Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold 20.3.0 Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet has been incorporated into Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold. Version 20.3.0 supports .NET 8, 9, 10 and 11. Install it as a .NET tool, not as a project package reference. The MVC and Design project packages use the separate fixed versions listed above; 20.3.0 is not a version of those packages. ### Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold 20.x Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold) | >= 20.0.0-preview.1.26156.3, <= 20.1.0 | 20.3.0 The 20.x tool contains the vulnerable Identity and Blazor templates for .NET 8.0 through 11.0. ### Affected legacy prereleases The following exact versions also contain affected templates: - [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc) and [Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design): `11.0.0-preview.1.26156.3` and `11.0.0-preview.1.26230.3`. - [Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet): `10.0.0-rc.1.25458.5` and `10.0.0-rc.1.25468.1`. Apply the generated-code repair below to applications created with these versions. For new scaffolding, use the Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold 20.3.0 tool, which supports .NET 8 through 11. Migrating to that tool is not an update to an MVC or Design project package reference and does not repair previously generated code. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Check both the installed scaffolding package/tool version and the code it generated. Applications generated with an affected template remain affected after the tool is updated unless their handlers are corrected. The `dotnet-aspnet-codegenerator` command loads generators from the application's dependencies. Check the project's Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design and Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGenerators.Mvc references against the versions above; updating only the command-line tool does not replace those project dependencies. For applications created with `dotnet new`, check the selected SDK with `dotnet --version` in the working directory. Use `dotnet new list` to identify available templates and `dotnet new uninstall` without arguments to list separately installed template packages. Web ProjectTemplates can be bundled with an SDK or installed separately; a project package reference alone does not identify which template generated the application. ### How do I fix the issue? Update affected scaffolding packages/tools and project dependencies to the patched versions above before generating additional code. Updating scaffolding packages/tools does not repair previously generated applications. Change generated ForgotPassword and ResendEmailConfirmation handlers, including Blazor equivalents, to send only to the stored email returned for the located user; reject missing stored addresses, rebuild and redeploy affected apps. For an existing global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold installation, update the tool: ```shell dotnet tool update --global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold --version 20.3.0 ``` For Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet installations, uninstall the old tool and install its replacement: ```shell dotnet tool uninstall --global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet dotnet tool install --global Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold --version 20.3.0 ``` For a new installation, use the install command alone. For local tools, use `--local` instead of `--global` and run the commands from the directory containing the tool manifest. Visual Studio installs and uses the updated scaffolding tool automatically; command-line installations must be updated separately. Visual Studio 17.14 uses the legacy CodeGeneration packages listed above; keep Visual Studio updated and check independently maintained project dependencies. For SDK-bundled templates, install and select an updated SDK that includes the corrected ProjectTemplates version; check `global.json` if an older SDK remains selected. Update separately installed template packs independently. Updating the SDK does not necessarily replace a separately installed template pack. For the affected legacy prereleases, correct the generated handlers before using or deploying the generated application. #### Manual repair for generated Identity handlers This repair also applies to applications generated with the affected 11.0 scaffolding packages and Microsoft.dotnet-scaffold-aspnet 10.0 RC versions above; it does not require migrating to a different scaffolding tool. In the generated `ForgotPassword` and `ResendEmailConfirmation` handlers, retain the existing user lookup, missing-user responses, password-reset confirmation checks, token generation and callback-URL encoding. After those user checks, retrieve the email from the located account before sending: ```csharp var storedEmail = await UserManager.GetEmailAsync(user); if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(storedEmail)) { throw new InvalidOperationException("Users must have an email."); } ``` In Razor Pages handlers, use `_userManager` instead of `UserManager`. Replace only the recipient argument `Input.Email` with `storedEmail` in `_emailSender.SendEmailAsync`, `EmailSender.SendPasswordResetLinkAsync` and `EmailSender.SendConfirmationLinkAsync`, as applicable. Keep `Input.Email` for the account lookup; do not use it as the message recipient. Apply the change to both handlers, including their Blazor equivalents, then rebuild and redeploy. Reapply the repair if affected templates generate the handlers again. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/Scaffolding. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Issues.Body: > **Announcement consolidated:** See the [November 2026 .NET Runtime security announcement](https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/498) and [shared feedback thread](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/137280). This original CVE post is retained for existing links. Closing it does not withdraw the advisory or its remediation guidance. ## Executive Summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-120778 - Aspire Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in the Aspire CLI. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. An insecure temporary directory used by Aspire CLI-generated builds can allow a local attacker to influence MSBuild response-file discovery and execute code with the privileges of the developer running the CLI. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/aspire/issues/22101 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.3 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-379 (Creation of Temporary File in Directory with Insecure Permissions) - **MSRC severity:** Important ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** x64, Arm64 ## Affected Packages ### Standalone Aspire CLI Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Aspire.Cli](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli) | >= 13.2.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.linux-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.linux-x64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.linux-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.linux-arm64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.linux-musl-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.linux-musl-x64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.osx-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.osx-x64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.osx-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.osx-arm64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 ### Aspire CLI npm packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [@microsoft/aspire-cli](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-x64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-x64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-arm64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-arm64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-musl-x64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-musl-x64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-x64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-x64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-arm64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-arm64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 The affected scenario concerns CLI-generated server and integration builds on non-Windows systems when a local attacker can influence automatic MSBuild response-file discovery through an attacker-writable directory. This includes builds started by `aspire sdk generate`, `aspire sdk dump`, and `aspire sdk export`. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? The reported scenario involves a local attacker influencing a generated build through a shared temporary-directory ancestor while another user invokes the Aspire CLI. Versions 13.2.0 through 13.6.4 are affected. Aspire ships independently of .NET. Installing a .NET runtime or SDK update does not establish that the affected Aspire CLI has been updated. ### How do I fix the issue? Update the Aspire CLI to version 13.6.5 or later. If installed as a .NET tool, update the Aspire.Cli package. If installed using npm, update @microsoft/aspire-cli to version 13.6.5 or later; its platform-specific dependency must also resolve to version 13.6.5 or later. Otherwise update the CLI through its installation method. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue in the [Aspire repository](https://github.com/microsoft/aspire). ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-120778](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-120778) ### Acknowledgements - l8BL with [ENKI WhiteHat](https://enki.co.kr/) ### Revisions V1.0 (November 10, 2026): Advisory published.

Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in the Aspire CLI. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. Insecure temporary files used by Aspire CLI can allow a local attacker to obtain sensitive configuration information. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/aspire/issues/22100 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.3 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:L/A:L` - **Weakness:** CWE-532 (Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File) - **MSRC severity:** Important - **Impact:** Information Disclosure ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** x64, Arm64 ## Affected Packages ### Standalone Aspire CLI Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- Aspire CLI ([Aspire.Cli](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli)) | >= 13.2.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.linux-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.linux-x64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.linux-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.linux-arm64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.linux-musl-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.linux-musl-x64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.osx-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.osx-x64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Cli.osx-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Cli.osx-arm64) | >= 13.3.0, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 ### Aspire CLI npm packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [@microsoft/aspire-cli](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-x64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-x64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-arm64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-arm64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-musl-x64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-linux-musl-x64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-x64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-x64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-arm64](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@microsoft/aspire-cli-osx-arm64) | >= 13.4.2, < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 The affected component is the Aspire CLI's deprecated MCP configuration scanner, which ships in the CLI packages listed above. Its temporary-file diagnostics can include configuration content and use a fixed path in a shared temporary directory. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? The reported scenario involves running Aspire CLI agent or MCP initialization commands on a non-Windows system with a temporary directory shared by multiple users. Versions 13.2.0 through 13.6.4 are affected. Aspire ships independently of .NET. Installing a .NET runtime or SDK update does not establish that the affected Aspire CLI has been updated. ### How do I fix the issue? Update the Aspire CLI to version 13.6.5 or later. If installed as a .NET tool, update the Aspire.Cli package. If installed using npm, update @microsoft/aspire-cli to version 13.6.5 or later; its platform-specific dependency must also resolve to version 13.6.5 or later. Otherwise update the CLI through its installation method. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. SignalR connections are not consistently bound to the identity negotiated at connection establishment, allowing injected messages to execute Hub invocations as the victim. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/discussions/70467 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Critical - **Score:** 9.0 (base score) - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-863 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Windows, Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** All ## Affected Packages The tables list affected version ranges and fixed package versions. Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-120006 - Aspire Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in Aspire. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. Disclosure of an Aspire Dashboard authentication cookie to a linked service can allow an attacker-controlled container to replay the authenticated session and execute code as the host developer. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/microsoft/aspire/issues/22092 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.5 - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H` - **Weakness:** CWE-201 (Insertion of Sensitive Information Into Sent Data) ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** macOS - **Architectures:** x64, Arm64 ## Affected Packages ### Standalone Aspire Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Aspire.Hosting.AppHost](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Hosting.AppHost) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 [Aspire.Hosting](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Aspire.Hosting) | < 13.6.5 | 13.6.5 The affected scenario involves a Dashboard-authenticated AppHost workflow with an attacker-controlled container and a linked HTTPS YARP gateway. The affected hosting code is in `Aspire.Hosting`, a dependency of `Aspire.Hosting.AppHost`. `Aspire.AppHost.Sdk` supplies the AppHost package implicitly unless the project overrides the default references. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? The reported scenario involves a developer starting an Aspire AppHost, authenticating to its Dashboard, and following a resource link that routes to an attacker-controlled container. All released versions through 13.6.4 are affected. Aspire ships independently of .NET. Installing a .NET runtime or SDK update does not establish that the affected Aspire components have been updated. ### How do I fix the issue? Update the AppHost project's `Aspire.Hosting.AppHost` package reference to version 13.6.5 or later. If the project obtains this package implicitly through `Aspire.AppHost.Sdk`, update that SDK reference to version 13.6.5 or later. Explicit package references or central version pins must also resolve `Aspire.Hosting` to version 13.6.5 or later. Restore dependencies, rebuild, and restart the AppHost after updating. Updating only the .NET runtime, .NET SDK, Aspire CLI, or standalone Dashboard does not replace the AppHost project's hosting dependencies. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue in the [Aspire repository](https://github.com/microsoft/aspire). ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Microsoft disclaims all warranties, either express or implied, including the warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-120006](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-120006) ### Acknowledgements - samthewhitehat ### Revisions V1.0 (November 10, 2026): Advisory published.

Issues.Title: Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-114155 - .NET Elevation of Privilege Vulnerability
Issues.Body: ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in the .NET SDK's dotnet-watch component. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected SDK installations. A local attacker who can replace or modify a temporary solution file used by dotnet-watch can alter a subsequent build. The fix stores generated solution files in a private temporary directory and keeps each file open with read-only sharing while the build uses it. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk/issues/57040 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** High - **Score:** 7.5 (base score) - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:L/AC:H/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:H/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-367 - **MSRC severity:** Important - **Impact:** Elevation of Privilege ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Linux, macOS. - **Architectures:** Linux: Arm, Arm64, x64; macOS: Arm64, x64 Windows is outside this advisory's affected scope when its temporary directory is private to the current user, as assumed by the implementation. Shared or insecurely configured Windows temporary directories are not covered by that assumption. ## Affected Packages The .NET SDK includes dotnet-watch and the Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch assembly. Each SDK feature band is a separate servicing line. Update an affected 10.0.3xx installation to the fixed 10.0.4xx SDK listed below. ### .NET SDK 10.0.3xx Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [.NET SDK (dotnet-watch) 10.0.3xx](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/10.0) | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.303 | 10.0.404 ### .NET SDK 10.0.4xx Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [.NET SDK (dotnet-watch) 10.0.4xx](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/10.0) | >= 10.0.400, <= 10.0.403 | 10.0.404 ### .NET SDK 11.0.1xx Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [.NET SDK (dotnet-watch) 11.0.1xx](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/11.0) | >= 11.0.100-preview.3.26207.106, <= 11.0.100-rc.3.26522.148 | 11.0.100 ### Separately restored Aspire watch tool Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire) | >= 10.0.300, <= 10.0.303 | 10.0.404 [Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire) | >= 10.0.400, <= 10.0.403 | 10.0.404 [Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire) | >= 11.0.100-preview.3.26207.106, <= 11.0.100-rc.3.26522.148 | 11.0.100 This tool has its own copy of the watch implementation. Updating the SDK does not necessarily replace a separately restored tool. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Run `dotnet --version` from the directory where you run dotnet-watch to identify the selected SDK. Use `dotnet --info` and `dotnet --list-sdks` to check its installation path, OS, architecture, and other installed SDKs. Check the nearest applicable `global.json`, including its `version` and `rollForward` settings: installing a newer SDK does not necessarily change the SDK selected for a pinned project. See [.NET SDK selection](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/versions/selection). Review use of dotnet-watch against the affected intervals above. Membership in a listed feature band alone does not establish that a specific SDK version is vulnerable. For Aspire or other tooling that separately restores Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire, check the actual restored package version separately from the selected SDK. ### How do I fix the issue? The fixed SDK versions are 10.0.404 and 11.0.100, as applicable. Update each affected SDK installation and restart dotnet-watch. For SDKs installed through Visual Studio, update Visual Studio to a release that includes a fixed SDK. Updating only an application runtime does not replace SDK-bundled tools. Ensure that `global.json` and its SDK roll-forward policy select a fixed SDK, then rerun `dotnet --version` in the working directory to verify the selection. The SDK-bundled watch tool is installed beneath that selected SDK's `DotnetTools/dotnet-watch` directory. If Microsoft.DotNet.HotReload.Watch.Aspire is restored separately, update its package reference or the consuming tool's version configuration to 10.0.404 or 11.0.100, as applicable, restore the tool, and restart the consuming process. An SDK update alone does not update that restored copy. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Further information can be found in the MSRC [Report an Issue FAQ](https://www.microsoft.com/msrc/faqs-report-an-issue). Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/sdk. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue. ### Disclaimer The information provided in this advisory is provided "as is" without warranty of any kind. Microsoft disclaims all warranties, either express or implied, including the warranties of merchantability and fitness for a particular purpose. In no event shall Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers be liable for any damages whatsoever including direct, indirect, incidental, consequential, loss of business profits or special damages, even if Microsoft Corporation or its suppliers have been advised of the possibility of such damages. Some states do not allow the exclusion or limitation of liability for consequential or incidental damages so the foregoing limitation may not apply. ### External Links [CVE-2026-114155](https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-114155) ### Acknowledgements - [Ky0toFu](https://x.com/ky0tofu) ### Revisions V1.0 (November 10, 2026): Advisory published.

Each advisory below remains the authoritative source for its affected versions and remediation. The fixes and required actions differ by CVE; a runtime or SDK update does not replace every standalone package or repair every application. **Feedback:** [Use the shared .NET Runtime feedback thread](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/137280). Original CVE-2026-118746 advisory details (preserved) ## Executive summary Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in .NET. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components. Unix Negotiate authentication can accept a request when required channel-binding information is missing. ## Discussion Discussion for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/137280 ## CVSS Details - **Version:** 3.1 - **Severity:** Medium - **Score:** 6.8 (base score) - **Vector:** `CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:R/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N/E:U/RL:O/RC:C` - **Weakness:** CWE-636 ## Affected Platforms - **Platforms:** Linux, macOS - **Architectures:** Arm, Arm64, x64 ## Affected Packages The tables list affected .NET 11 runtime package versions and fixed versions. The issue occurs during server-side Negotiate authentication with `PolicyEnforcement.Always` when the client omits the channel-binding token. ### .NET 11.0 - Linux runtime packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-arm](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-arm) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, < [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-musl-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-musl-arm64) | > 11.0.0-preview.7.26381.103, < 11.0.0 | 11.0.0 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-musl-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-musl-x64) | > 11.0.0-preview.7.26381.103, < 11.0.0 | 11.0.0 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-x64) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, < 11.0.0-preview.7.26381.103 | 11.0.0 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.linux-x64) | > 11.0.0-preview.7.26381.103, < 11.0.0 | 11.0.0 The six Linux runtime packages at version 11.0.0-preview.7.26381.103 reject `PolicyEnforcement.Always` before authentication and are not affected. ### .NET 11.0 - macOS runtime packages Package | Affected version | Patched version --- | --- | --- [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.osx-arm64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.osx-arm64) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, < 11.0.0-preview.7.26381.103 | 11.0.0 [Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.osx-x64](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Microsoft.NETCore.App.Runtime.osx-x64) | >= 11.0.0-preview.1, < 11.0.0-preview.7.26381.103 | 11.0.0 The macOS runtime packages at versions 11.0.0-preview.7.26381.103, 11.0.0-rc.1.26425.128, 11.0.0-rc.2.26504.105, and 11.0.0-rc.3.26522.148 reject `PolicyEnforcement.Always` before authentication and are not affected. ## Advisory FAQ ### How do I know if I am affected? Applications using server-side Negotiate authentication with `PolicyEnforcement.Always` are affected when their runtime package version is in the platform-specific ranges above. On Linux, this includes .NET 11 previews 1 through 6 and release candidates 1 through 3. On macOS, this includes .NET 11 previews 1 through 6. Preview 7 is not affected on either platform, and macOS release candidates 1 through 3 are not affected. Self-contained applications include their own runtime; updating a machine-wide runtime does not replace it. ### How do I fix the issue? For affected Linux and macOS .NET 11 prereleases, install .NET 11.0.0 or update each independently referenced runtime package to 11.0.0. Restart applications. Rebuild and redeploy self-contained applications; updating a machine-wide runtime does not replace their embedded runtime. An SDK update alone does not update an application's standalone package references. On macOS, `PolicyEnforcement.Always` remains unsupported and throws `PlatformNotSupportedException`. The update prevents authentication from proceeding without the required protection; it does not add Extended Protection support on macOS. ## Other Information ### Reporting Security Issues If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the [MSRC Researcher Portal](https://msrc.microsoft.com/report/vulnerability/new). Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty. ### Support You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. > This issue is a locked mirror of https://github.com/dotnet/core/discussions/10711. See that thread for discussion.

We are pleased to announce the general availability of .NET 11.

Read about the final release in the [.NET Blog announcement](https://devblogs.microsoft.com/dotnet/announcing-dotnet-11/).

This release includes C# 15, faster developer tools, runtime and library improvements, and new capabilities for web, mobile, desktop, and AI apps. Explore the full release notes below.

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/sdk.md)

## 📱 .NET MAUI

* [Full Release Notes](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/11.0.0/dotnetmaui.md)

## 🖥️ Windows Presentation Foundation (WPF)

## 🚀 Get started

To get started with .NET 11, [install the .NET 11 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/11.0).

If you're on Windows using Visual Studio, use an up-to-date [Visual Studio 2026](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/vs/) installation that supports .NET 11.

You can also use Visual Studio Code and the [C# Dev Kit](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-dotnettools.csdevkit) extension with .NET 11.

Before upgrading an existing application, review the [breaking changes in .NET 11](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/compatibility/11), update your target frameworks and dependencies, and run your tests.

Celebrate the release of .NET 11 at [.NET Conf 2026](https://dot.net/conf), November 10-13.

## 🔔 Stay up-to-date with .NET 11

You can stay up-to-date with all the features of .NET 11 with:

* [What's new in WPF](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/desktop/wpf/whats-new/net110)
* [Breaking changes in .NET 11](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/compatibility/11)
* [.NET 11 releases](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/README.md)

Be sure to subscribe to the GitHub Discussions [RSS news feed](https://github.com/dotnet/core/discussions/categories/news.atom) for all release announcements.
